title: Finite locally free projective bundles and tautological base change
statement:
Let $B$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $n\geq0$, and $F$ a locally free $\mathcal O_B$-module of constant rank $n+1$ [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. Put $P=\operatorname{Proj}_B(\operatorname{Sym}^{\bullet}F)$ with projection $p:P\to B$, using the symmetric algebra sheaf [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra] with the symmetric grading [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded] and relative Proj [def-nagata-relative-proj]. The degree-one twisting module $\mathcal O_P(1)$, obtained on each affine base open from the shifted graded module [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] $\operatorname{Sym}^{\bullet}(F)(1)$ and glued by homogeneous localization, is invertible [def-sc-invertible-module]. The morphism $p$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Every frame of $F|_U$ identifies $(P|_U,\mathcal O_P(1)|_{P|_U})$ with $(\mathbf P^n_U,\mathcal O(1))$, where projective space is [def-nagata-relative-projective-space] and its twist has transition functions $e_i=(T_i/T_j)e_j$ [def-pc-projective-space-twist]. For any scheme morphism $g:B'\to B$, there is a canonical isomorphism
$$\mathbf P_{B'}(g^*F)\cong B'\times_B P$$
carrying its degree-one twisting module to the pullback of $\mathcal O_P(1)$. These isomorphisms respect identities and composition. On $\mathbf P^n_K$ over any field $K$, with coordinates $T_0,\ldots,T_n$ and $n\geq1$, the subscheme $T_0=0$ is $\mathbf P^{n-1}_K$, its complement is $\mathbf A^n_K$ with coordinates $t_i=T_i/T_0$, and each divisor $T_i=0$ has associated line bundle $\mathcal O(1)$. The intersection $T_1=\cdots=T_n=0$ is the reduced point $[1:0:\cdots:0]$ in that affine chart. For $n=0$, $p$ is an isomorphism and $\mathcal O_P(1)$ corresponds to $F$.

proof.text: Choose the family of normalized frame models from [lem-pur-projective-bundle-frame-models]. Use [lem-pur-projective-bundle-base-change-coherence] for the identity- and composition-compatible coefficient and degree-one twist comparisons. These are separate parts of the original chart construction.

Choose a trivializing open cover of F. On each inverse-image open its twist is the pullback of the invertible polynomial twist, so it is invertible globally by locality of finite local freeness of rank one. Each restricted structural morphism is a composition of two chart isomorphisms and the proper projective-space projection, so properness descends by target locality. Finite local freeness of the same rank is preserved by tensor pullback, using the canonical comparison to adjoint pullback.

For n=0 each chart structural morphism is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-zero-isomorphism]; target locality gives an isomorphism globally. On each frame chart the sole free-basis inclusion is an isomorphism. The normalized frame quotient is a free generator on the whole one-coordinate standard chart, hence an isomorphism. Cancel the source trivialization to see that the restricted universal quotient is an isomorphism. Reflect isomorphisms along the jointly surjective flat family of open immersions using [lem-sc-flat-cover-module-isomorphism-reflection]. Its inverse identifies L with p^*F.

Use [lem-pur-projective-bundle-coordinate-geometry] for the independent polynomial field-coordinate assertions. Assemble the frame models, the proved properness and invertibility, the coherent comparisons, pullback ranks, coordinate geometry and proved rank-zero assertions into the required system. Select its realization at B,F; the selection equation is reflexivity. No geometric clause is dropped.
